 At the Council workshop held on January 27, 2025, David Elliot presented a proposal for the development of an Emergency and Disaster Preparedness Plan for the Town of Taos. Following this presentation and subsequent discussion, a formal proposal was submitted to engage Emergency Management consulting services. 

 A Sole Source determination for these services was submitted to the State of New Mexico on March 15, 2025, and was publicly posted on the State’s procurement website for the required 30-day period. No protests were received during this time. The Town’s Procurement Office has reviewed the proposal and has approved the Sole Source determination.

matters.title: A. Discussion, consideration, and possible approval of Quote No. 72719 from JWC Environmental to rebuild the bandscreens at the Taos Wastewater Treatment Facility in the amount of $85,308.36, exclusive of New Mexico gross receipts tax. This purchase utilizes sole source procurement No. 40-M0093-24-C
matters.text:
Agenda Item Details 

 Meeting 
 Feb 10, 2026 - Town Council Regular Meeting 
 Category 
 6. Matters from Staff 
 Subject 
 A. Discussion, consideration, and possible approval of Quote No. 72719 from JWC Environmental to rebuild the bandscreens at the Taos Wastewater Treatment Facility in the amount of $85,308.36, exclusive of New Mexico gross receipts tax. This purchase utilizes sole source procurement No. 40-M0093-24-CP209. (Public Works Director Reynold Vasquez) 
 Type 
 Action 
 Preferred Date 
 Feb 10, 2026 
 Absolute Date 
 Feb 10, 2026 
 Fiscal Impact 
 Yes 
 Dollar Amount 
 83,865.00 
 Budgeted 
 Yes 
 Budget Source 
 6300-4301-42005 - $85,308.36 + $1,550.00 (7.75% tax on labor only); Total: $86,858.36 
 Recommended Action 
 Approval 

 1. Summary/Background: 

 Critical Infrastructure: The fine screens (bandscreens) at the Headworks of the Wastewater Treatment Facility (WWTF) are vital to ongoing plant operations and essential for protecting critical equipment.
 Operational Risk: Continuous band screening protects membranes and ensures the plant meets effluent quality standards required for compliance. Equipment failure jeopardizes both objectives.
 Financial Risk: Failure could result in the costly, premature replacement of membrane modules every 2 to 3 years, rather than the typical 7 to 10+ years. Membrane modules and cassettes were replaced in March 2024 and October 2025, at a total cost of $2,115,103.15, to ensure continued reliable service for the community.

 2. Immediate/Interim Action: Bandscreen Rehabilitation 

 To mitigate the immediate risk and ensure compliance until funding and procurement of a permanent solution are secured, an interim rehabilitation of the existing bandscreens is recommended.

 3. Next Steps - Path to Permanent Bandscreen Replacement 

 Repairing the screens immediately is a temporary but necessary step. Full replacement is planned as the permanent solution.

 Staff are securing engineering services for the permanent replacement of the fine screen. Staff is working with Waterworks Engineering to obtain a quote for engineering services to draft the full scope of work, including design, project management, bidding, and construction-phase services to replace the screens. 
 Waterworks Engineering visited the WWTF on January 22, 2026, to gather data and will provide the 3D facility scans.

 Staff requests Council approval of the $85,308.36 quote from JWC Environmental (excluding New Mexico gross receipts tax), which is urgently needed to mitigate operational and compliance risks until the permanent replacement is complete.

 §

 Category 
 5. Matters from Staff 
 Subject 
 C. Discussion, consideration, and possible approval of Resolution 26-17, a resolution requesting to dispose of obsolete, worn-out or unused tangible personal property. (Chief Procurement Officer Bailey Andrea) 
 Type 
 Action 

 Summary/Background: Staff is requesting approval to declare certain Town-owned assets as surplus property and authorize their disposal through public auction. The items include the existing ice rink batter boards and glass system being removed as part of the ice rink renovation project, as well as a Town-owned truck that is no longer in service. Retaining these assets would require unnecessary storage space and ongoing maintenance without providing operational benefit to the Town. Disposal through public auction is recommended in accordance with Town surplus property procedures and NM DFA asset management guidance to ensure transparency and proper stewardship of public assets.

 The Town requires specialized emergency management consulting services to strengthen emergency preparedness, planning, response, recovery, and grant compliance efforts. Due to the specialized expertise, continuity of services, and unique qualifications required, staff determined that a sole source procurement was in the Town's best interest. Resilience Emergency Management, with David Elliot, has the experience and technical expertise necessary to provide these services and support the Town's emergency management program. Approval of this agreement will ensure the Town maintains preparedness for emergencies, supports regulatory compliance, and enhances the community's resilience while providing professional guidance for current and future emergency management initiatives. Staff recommends approval of the sole source procurement and subsequent contract as being in the best interest of the Town.
